slices.focus: Tasha introduces herself and her life goal: Bereavement Care Reach
slices.summary: Tasha provides a comprehensive self-introduction covering her identity (37, Raleigh, ISFJ), work (bereavement coordinator at Transitions LifeCare, 7th year), and her five-year goal called Bereavement Care Reach — building Wake County bereavement follow-up into a consistent countywide program with 45+ trained volunteers and six recurring grief-support groups. She describes her stress patterns (insomnia, jaw clenching), living situation (single, one-bedroom apartment), budget constraints ($62k salary, student loans), and key relationships: aunt Denise Alston, friend Imani Brooks, supervisor Renee Holloway, and work colleagues Miriam Sloan and Caleb Jennings. She shares preferences for 90s R&B, Southern fiction, and quiet cabin travel.

Adopting an older cat — mentioned as eventual desire

slices.focus: Work tips from messy into crisis; Miriam gives Tasha one protected day for coverage triage
slices.summary: Tasha describes how two volunteer-led grief groups in east Raleigh nearly got canceled, prompting her to present Miriam with evidence from sign-in binders and referral emails. Miriam agrees to carve out one day a week for Tasha to focus on volunteer coverage triage and bereavement process cleanup, but without a promotion, extra staffing, or a rewritten job description. Tasha wrestles with the tension between feeling relieved to have protected time and concerned that her unofficial role is hardening without guardrails. The agent helps her plan a written scope, a simple tracking system starting with the east Raleigh groups, and a weekly update rhythm to prevent the protected day from becoming a catch-all.
open_loops: Written outline for Miriam — planned but not yet drafted
Spreadsheet and binder cleanup for east Raleigh groups — first pass pending
Volunteer confirmation and no-show reporting process — needs design

decisions: Miriam informally carved out one day each week for Tasha to lead volunteer coverage triage and bereavement process clean
